scenes.topic_description:
Situation: You arrive to view a rental apartment with an agent for the first time. This short exchange happens before you start walking through the flat and helps you understand the process and set expectations for the visit.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Agent.
Not in this scene: discussing the apartment in detail, asking about pet rules, rent, deposit, documents, making a decision.
must_say: say you are here for the viewing — slot: the apartment
give your name — slot: the name
ask how long the viewing will take — slot: none
ask which rooms you will see first — slot: the part of the apartment
explain what kind of place you need — slot: the requirement
ask whether there are other viewings today — slot: none
must_understand: asks whether you are here for a specific apartment
asks your name
says how the viewing will go and which rooms you will see
asks what you are looking for
says whether other people are viewing the place

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: You are walking through the apartment with the agent and need to decide whether the place could work for you. You have a small dog, so the pet rule is especially important, along with costs, condition, and practical details.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Agent.
Not in this scene: introductions and viewing plan, application steps, required documents, negotiating the contract, arranging the next contact.
must_say: ask what is included in the rent — slot: the thing included
ask whether a pet is allowed — slot: the pet
ask whether there are extra monthly costs — slot: the cost
ask how old something in the flat is — slot: the thing
explain a concern about the apartment — slot: the concern
ask whether something can be changed — slot: the change
ask about the neighbourhood — slot: the place nearby
confirm what matters most to you — slot: the priority
must_understand: says what is included in the rent and what is not
explains the building or flat rules about pets
says what extra monthly costs there are
explains whether changes are possible and under what conditions
tells you about the area or nearby services

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: The viewing is ending and you want to move forward if the apartment suits you. This interaction covers the application process, timing, and what you need to send after the visit to keep your chance of renting the place.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Agent.
Not in this scene: first introductions, detailed questions about the apartment, pet rules, room-by-room comments, discussing what is included in the rent.
must_say: say you are interested in the apartment — slot: the apartment
ask what documents are required — slot: the document type
ask when a decision will be made — slot: the decision
ask how to submit an application — slot: the application method
ask whether a holding deposit is needed — slot: the deposit
ask who will contact you next — slot: the person
confirm when you will send something — slot: the document
confirm how you will stay in touch — slot: the contact method
must_understand: says what documents you need to provide
explains how to apply and by when
says whether a deposit is needed and how it works
tells you when the landlord or agent will decide
gives the next contact step
